site.summary: microsoft-privacy-clone Clone of the Microsoft account privacy management panel and its sub-pages. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Main panel: top black Microsoft ribbon + account header (4-square logo + global nav + avatar); hero section with title and Privacy Checkup / Download / Privacy Statement entries; activity-data card grid (Browse / Search / Location / Voice / Media / Apps / Xbox / Ads — 8 cards total); privacy-settings toggle list (6 toggles with live "Saving…/Saved" feedback); two manage-data tiles (download / clear, clear has a modal second-confirmation); Microsoft product-level privacy entries (Windows / Xbox / Edge / Bing / Outlook / OneDrive / LinkedIn / M365) | | `browse-history.html` | Edge browse-history detail: breadcrumb, setting-status hint, filter bar (time range / device / search box), activity table (time / page title + URL / device / delete icon), per-row delete with animation, "Clear all" with modal confirmation, empty state | | `ad-settings.html` | Ad settings: master toggle (See ads that interest you) controls all sub-items; per-service cards (Microsoft / Bing & Edge / LinkedIn / Xbox) with independent toggles; multi-select intere

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the Microsoft privacy dashboard and its sub-pages, validating all interactive controls, state changes, destructive actions, and responsive layouts.
run_plan.summary: The exploration will proceed through four phases, starting with the main dashboard's toggles and cards, moving to the data detail pages (browse history and ad settings), then validating the multi-step data download flow, and finally re-checking critical interactions on a mobile viewport. Special attention will be given to toggle feedback, modal confirmations for destructive actions, and the master/sub-toggle relationship on the ad settings page.
assumptions: The site is a client-side clone; thus, data deletion and download submissions will not persist or result in real network success, but UI state changes (e.g., 'Saving…/Saved', modal appearances, row animations) must still occur and be validated.
The 6 privacy toggles on the main page and the master toggle on the ad settings page have functional client-side logic to show feedback.
The 'Clear all' actions on browse history and the main dashboard trigger the second-confirmation modals seen in the DOM summary.
risk_hotspots: Destructive actions: 'Clear all' buttons on index.html and browse-history.html must properly trigger confirmation modals and prevent accidental data loss.
Toggle feedback: The 6 privacy setting toggles on index.html must display the live 'Saving…/Saved' feedback without layout shifts.
Ad settings dependency: The master toggle 'See ads that interest you' must correctly disable/enable the dependent service toggles (Microsoft, Bing & Edge, LinkedIn, Xbox).
Mobile tap targets: The top navigation ribbons have been flagged for small tap targets (<44px height), which may cause severe usability issues on mobile viewports.

phases.title: Dashboard Overview & Privacy Toggles
phases.objective: Validate the main dashboard layout, activity cards, and the privacy settings toggle interactions with their live feedback.
key_checks: Verify the 8 activity data cards render correctly with their stats.
Toggle each of the 6 privacy settings off and on, verifying the 'Saving…' and 'Saved' feedback appears and resolves.
Click the 'Clear' button in the 'Manage your data' section and verify the second-confirmation modal appears and can be cancelled.
Check the hero section links (Privacy Checkup, Download your data, Privacy Statement, Help with privacy) for correct navigation or hover states.
exit_criteria: All 6 toggles have been flipped and their feedback validated.
Clear data modal has been triggered and dismissed.

phases.title: Browse History Detail & Deletion
phases.objective: Validate the browse history filtering, individual row deletion, and bulk clear functionality.
key_checks: Use the filter bar (Time range, Device) and verify the activity table updates or appears to filter.
Delete an individual history row using the delete icon and verify the removal animation.
Click 'Clear all browse history' and verify the modal confirmation appears.
Dismiss the modal, then confirm the clear action to check for the empty state UI.
Navigate back to the dashboard using the breadcrumb link.
exit_criteria: Filters interacted with and table state observed.
Clear all modal triggered, dismissed, and accepted; empty state verified.

phases.title: Ad Settings & Data Download Flow
phases.objective: Validate the master/dependent toggle relationship in ad settings and the multi-step form inputs in the data download flow.
key_checks: Toggle the master 'See ads that interest you' off and verify that the per-service cards (Microsoft, Bing, LinkedIn, Xbox) become disabled or unchecked.
Re-enable the master toggle and interact with an individual service toggle.
On download-data.html, step through the 4 sections: select data categories, select time range, select delivery method, and attempt to submit/confirm.
Verify that the form inputs (checkboxes for categories, radio buttons for time/delivery) respond correctly to clicks.
exit_criteria: Master toggle dependency on ad-settings.html verified.
All steps of the download form interacted with and visual state changes confirmed.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Validation
phases.objective: Re-validate critical flows and check for layout regressions and tap target usability on a mobile viewport.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport and check the top navigation ribbon for layout wrapping or overflow issues.
Verify the small tap targets identified in the prescan (e.g., 'Microsoft', 'Support', 'Sign out') and assess if they are too close together.
Interact with a privacy toggle on the main dashboard to ensure it works on mobile without layout shift.
Navigate to browse-history.html and verify the activity table is responsive (e.g., horizontal scroll or stacked cards) and the 'Clear all' button is accessible.
exit_criteria: Mobile viewport layout inspected on main pages.
Tap target severity assessed in mobile context.
Core toggle and modal interactions confirmed functional on mobile.

coverage_targets.pages: visit and interact with all 4 known HTML pages
coverage_targets.features: exercise all toggles, filter controls, modal triggers, and form inputs across the site
coverage_targets.mobile: validate layout, tap targets, and critical interactions (toggles, modals) on mobile viewport

notes: Pay close attention to the transition animations (e.g., row deletion in browse history) and ensure they do not cause layout jumps.
The prescan flagged multiple small tap targets in the header; during the mobile phase, explicitly check if these links are collapsed into a hamburger menu or remain problematic.

observation.title: Privacy dashboard | Microsoft account
observation.visible_text: Microsoft Support Software Devices Gaming Sign out Microsoft account Home Devices Subscriptions Payments & billing Privacy Security Rewards Order history Jack Wilson jack@outlook.com JW Privacy dashboard Review and manage the data Microsoft saves to make your experience better. You can view your activity, change privacy settings, or download a copy of your data at any time. Take the Privacy Checkup Download your data Privacy Statement Help with privacy Your activity data Some products and services save activity to your Microsoft account so it can sync across your devices. You can view and clear that data here. Browse history Microsoft Edge syncs the websites you visit so you can pick up where you left off across devices. 847 entries in the last 30 days Manage browse activity b Search history Bing remembers your searches to give you faster, more personal results next time you search. 312 searches in the last 30 days Manage search activity Location activity When location is on, your devices and Microsoft services can use your location to show local results. observation.title: Download your data | Privacy dashboard | Microsoft account
observation.visible_text: Microsoft Support Software Devices Gaming Microsoft account Home Devices Subscriptions Payments & billing Privacy Security Jack Wilson jack@outlook.com JW Privacy dashboard›Download your data Download your data Get a copy of the data Microsoft has saved for your account. We’ll package it as a downloadable archive and email you when it’s ready — usually within a few hours, but it can take up to 30 days. ⓘ This won’t delete any data. To remove activity instead, go back to the privacy dashboard. 1 · What to include Choose which categories of data should be in your archive. You can include everything or pick specific items. Account profile Name, contact info, sign-in history Browse activity Edge sync history Search activity Bing search history Location history Places associated with your account Voice recordings Saved samples used to improve recognition Media activity Movies, TV, music history Outlook contacts People and groups OneDrive metadata File list and sharing history (not file contents) Xbox & gaming Games, achievements, friends Ad preferences Topics and personalization state Select all · Clear all 2 · Time range How far back should we look? Older activity may have already been auto-deleted. Range All available history Last 12 months Last 90 days Last 30 days Custom range… 3 · How to deliver it We’ll send a secure download link to one of the email addresses on your account. Email jack@outlook.com (primary) jack.wilson@live.com Archive format .zip (recommended) .tar.gz The link expires after 14 days. Anyone with the link can download your archive — keep it private. 4 · Confirm I understand Microsoft will keep this archive on its servers for up to 14 days, and that downloading it doesn’t delete anything from my account. See the Privacy Statement. Request my data Cancel Privacy Terms of use Contact Microsoft © 2026 Microsoft · Local demo clone for UXBench.
